newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Heavy fighting erupts in northern Sri Lanka.
newsitem.headline: Heavy fighting erupts in northern Sri Lanka.

text.p: Heavy hand-to-hand fighting erupted overnight after Tamil Tiger rebels counter-attacked security forces consolidating their positions in a northern Sri Lankan town, military officials said on Saturday.
"There was bitter, hand-to-hand fighting on Friday night in the centre of Omanthai town," a military official said.
Some 100 rebels and 20 soldiers were killed in the counter-attack while more than 100 guerrillas and 40 soldiers were wounded, military officials said.
The military spokesman said he had no more details of the fighting and a spokesman for the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels was not immediately available for comment.

Troops captured Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, on Wednesday and began pushing further north on Friday, heading towards the heavily fortified rebel-held town of Puliyankulam, military officials said.
Friday's battle, in a housing project in the centre of town, began after a visit to northern Vavuniya by Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte, they said.
The Tigers used suicide cadres to destroy two armoured vehicles during the counter-attack in the town, they added.
Fighting died down in the evening but resumed with renewed intensity in the night, they said.

Troops based in Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, backed by artillery, tanks and helicopter gunships, launched the offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", on Tuesday.
Hospital officials said some 320 soldiers wounded in the past two days of fighting had been warded in hospitals in northern Anuradhapura and Jaffna, and also in the capital Colombo.
The LTTE's clandestine Voice of Tigers radio station, monitored by Reuters, said on Saturday 24 fighters had been killed in the first three days of fighting.
The Defence Ministry has said that up to Friday 27 soldiers had been killed and 31 wounded in the fighting.
It has also said that troops monitoring LTTE transmissions confirmed that at least 100 rebels had been killed or wounded in the battle for Omanthai alone.

The Defence Ministry says the main aim of the drive is to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni region from the LTTE, who are waging a war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
Analysts said the offensive aims to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya in north-central Sri Lanka with the Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops are heading.
But the LTTE has accused the military of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the guise of opening a supply route.
Vavuniya residents said that army artillery, firing from their bases in and around the town, had bombarded rebel positions on Friday while bombers and helicopters were heard flying over the town.
"The whole of Friday the army fired shells from the Vavuniya base," a resident said. "They are pounding LTTE areas. We heard explosions in the distance."
A pitched battle was also fought on Friday near Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, where troops advancing along an eastern flanks were attacked by the rebels.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
